name: Didier Deschamps
scopeNote: Counted spell proposed by the researcher: France national team, appointed Sunday 8 July 2012 (FFF announcement, Maxifoot same day; Blanc left after Euro 2012) to his 185th and last match, the 6-4 third-place play-off defeat to England on 18 July 2026 (Reuters/TimesLive 19 July). The brief expected an end in November 2026; sources show the tenure ended in July 2026 (Al Jazeera, 28 July, says it ended 'two weeks' before Zidane's appointment, roughly consistent). Raw results: 185 matches, 120 wins, 2018 World Cup, 2020-21 Nations League, Euro 2016 and 2022 World Cup finals. Monaco 2001-05 (Champions League final 2004), Juventus 2006-07 and Marseille 2009-12 are excluded: no tier A-B tactical coverage was found for them in this run and the national-team spell has the richest evidence. Excluded-spell dates are partial (month only, not verified in this run). The style is described by sources as pragmatic and result-first: a compact, deep mid/low block, ceding possession, quick vertical counters through Mbappe, set-piece work, 4-2-3-1 base (2014-2022), moving to back-three/five-man variants from 2021; 'defensive' is a press label, he himself rejects possession for its own sake. No source found states zonal vs man-marking at set pieces for France; only a 2016 pundit comparison implying man-marking. Evidence is mostly 2018 and 2022; 2012-17 and 2023-26 coverage is thin.
openQuestions: Spells proposed by the researcher and flagged: only France 2012-2026 counted; Monaco 2001-05, Juventus 2006-07 and Marseille 2009-12 excluded for lack of mined tactical evidence. Confirm or ask for a club-spell pass.

End date: 2026-07-18 (last match) used; brief expected November 2026, which no source supports. Al Jazeera says the tenure ended 'two weeks' before the 28 July announcement, slightly earlier than 18 July; FFF tribute dated 19 July.
Zonal vs man-marking at set pieces for France is not documented in any source read; Maxifoot 2016 only has a pundit (Boumsong) proposing a return to zonal, implying individual marking in 2016.
Euro 2024 and 2026 World Cup tactics (loss to Spain in semi-final, 6-4 loss to England) are not covered by tier A-B sources here (ESPN and UEFA pages failed).

Mourinhismo exemplar link: result-first pragmatism, deep block and set-piece work are well supported; 'adapting to the opponent' is supported by the 2018 Uruguay and Belgium set-piece adjustments and the 2021 half-time reshape.

sources.title: France National Team: Tactical Analysis (MBP School)
sources.evidence: The initial set-up of the side usually fluctuates between two different systems: the GK-4-3-3 and the GK-5-2-1-2. Depending on the players available and the opposition, Deschamps varies between the two, but always maintains the same general principles of play.

sources.title: France National Team: Tactical Analysis (MBP School)
sources.evidence: In terms of the dynamic organisation of the team in the defensive phase, France usually maintain the same structure as their base formation. Depending on the height of one of the central midfielders, they play a GK-5-3-2 or GK-5-2-1-2, or a GK-4-3-3 when they play with a line of four defenders at the back.

sources.title: France National Team: Tactical Analysis (MBP School)
sources.evidence: For this reason, the French coach seeks to accumulate a lot of players in the central channel, leaving the wings free for the wingers or full backs depending on the base structure he uses from the start.

sources.title: France National Team: Tactical Analysis (MBP School)
sources.evidence: Another of the team’s characteristics in the offensive phase is the role played by players such as Griezmann and Nkunku. In their teams, both usually operate as strikers, but in the national team they act as attacking midfielders, playing a very important role in the moments of dynamic build-up and progression of the play.

sources.title: France National Team: Tactical Analysis (MBP School)
sources.evidence: Although Deschamps always tries to prioritise 3+1 behind the ball in order to rationally protect space in the event of a turnover, France are also physically imposing.

sources.title: France National Team: Tactical Analysis (MBP School)
sources.evidence: regardless of the dynamic organisation they use, Deschamps’ team has a tendency to create defensive sub-blocks, i.e. to split into two blocks of players, forming a first block of eight players plus the goalkeeper, and another block of two players further forward, who are alert to a possible defence-attack transition.

sources.title: Behind France's World Cup 2022 campaign (Halfspaces)
sources.evidence: When teams attack France, they press very little, set up in a mid-block, and prefer to sit deeper.

sources.title: Behind France's World Cup 2022 campaign (Halfspaces)
sources.evidence: France, however, are not a possession-heavy team. France prefer to hit teams on the counter, where Griezmann and Dembelé can cut through defences to find Giroud and Mbappé

sources.title: Behind France's World Cup 2022 campaign (Halfspaces)
sources.evidence: if France need a late goal, Deschamps subs on Marcus Thuram, who is a useful outlet on the left, with Mbappé playing as a number 9. This was a key substitution that also led to France’s second goal vs Morocco.

sources.title: Behind France's World Cup 2022 campaign (Halfspaces)
sources.evidence: France’s formations vary from 2-4-4 to 2-3-5. Varane and Upamecano remain at the back to aid in the build-up

sources.title: Behind France's World Cup 2022 campaign (Halfspaces)
sources.evidence: Hernandez and Koundé push forward, providing width.
